Basal Cell Carcinoma
A common type of skin cancer that is the subject of the text.

Ultraviolet Radiation
A form of radiation that can damage DNA in skin cells and is a major risk factor for basal cell carcinoma.

DNA
The genetic material in skin cells that can be damaged by ultraviolet radiation.

Skin Cells
Cells in the skin that can be damaged by ultraviolet radiation, potentially leading to cancer.

Organ Transplant Recipients
Individuals who have received organ transplants and take immunosuppressive medicines.

Immunosuppressive Medicines
Medications taken by organ transplant recipients to prevent graft rejection, which weaken immune surveillance.

Immunosuppression
The state of weakened immune surveillance resulting from immunosuppressive medicines, increasing the risk of basal cell carcinoma.

Mohs Surgery
A surgical technique that removes thin layers of cancer-containing skin, commonly used for high-risk basal cell carcinoma in cosmetically sensitive areas.
